Article Title: Experts say AI may change the price of food and groceries: What is good and bad for customers
Article Text:
How AI is entering the grocery aisles and popular food chains

What experts say about dynamic pricing

What is good and bad for shoppers

Food retailers are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to run their operations. While the technology promises inventory efficiency and targeted discounts, economists and legal scholars warn it could also usher in an era of personalised and dynamic pricing – fundamentally altering what shoppers pay for everyday essentials.According to CNBC, retailers worldwide are testing and expanding data-driven systems at multiple touchpoints. US grocer Kroger introduced FlashFood, an AI platform that spots perishable items nearing their expiration dates, reduces their prices, and notifies shoppers via an app. Major chains in the US, including Kroger, Walmart, Whole Foods and Amazon Fresh are also rolling out digital screens to replace paper price tags, as are UK grocers Tesco, Morrisons and Asda. These digital tags enable stores to update shelf prices remotely in seconds.Financial platform Revolut recently tested facial-recognition checkouts at select coffee shops, letting buyers pay with a glance. In the UK, Sainsbury’s launched “SmartLists,” an AI tool that converts photos or meal ideas into curated shopping lists.Recently, an antitrust lawsuit accused McDonald’s of using an AI-driven “pricing engine” to determine menu rates across US stores and allegedly overcharge customers for staples like Big Macs and french fries.McDonald’s denied using AI to calculate what individual customers are willing to spend, asserting that it merely offers franchisees "tools, resources, research and recommendations to help them make informed decisions. "As automated infrastructure expands, experts caution that retailers have the tools to adjust pricing in real time based on demand patterns.“Dynamic pricing means changing prices in response to changing market conditions, such as demand, timing, capacity or competitors’ prices. It is not new. Airlines, hotels, and ride-hailing services have used it for years,” Miroslava Marinova, senior lecturer of commercial law at the University of East London, was quoted as saying.However, the rapid collection of granular personal data, which includes purchase records, browsing history, device location and buying routines, is beginning to blur the lines between broad market shifts and personal profiles.“Dynamic pricing responds primarily to market conditions, whereas personalised pricing uses information about the consumer to estimate willingness to pay. As retailers combine market-level information with increasingly detailed consumer data, the boundary between dynamic and personalised pricing becomes thinner,” Marinova explained.Algorithmic pricing is not inherently harmful to household budgets, the report said. Algorithms can lower prices on overstocked or aging inventory, curbing food waste and offering cheaper options for budget-conscious buyers. As a result, when discounts are applied strategically, certain foods and grocery services become more accessible to lower-income segments.However, there are some risks involved. The downside of individual-level pricing models centers on transparency and market fairness. When prices fluctuate continuously, shoppers cannot tell whether a price tag reflects general market supply or their personal browsing profile.“If consumers cannot understand why they received a particular price, cannot compare it with prices offered to others, and cannot effectively switch to another supplier, the normal disciplining effect of consumer choice becomes weaker,” Marinova warned.The Bank of England economists pointed out that when prices change constantly and differently for every shopper, measuring inflation becomes difficult.
Article Summary: Food retailers are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to run their operations. While the technology promises inventory efficiency and targeted discounts, economists and legal scholars warn it could usher in an era of personalised and dynamic pricing. Algorithms can lower prices on overstocked or aging inventory, curbing food waste and offering cheaper options for budget- conscious buyers.

Article Title: Apple launches Special Edition AirPods 5 in India with custom Rangoli design: Price, offers and more
Article Text:
Special Edition Apple AirPods 5

Other festive offers announced by Apple

Apple has opened its festive season in India with a Special Edition AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, the first of its kind, engraved with a custom Rangoli design. The limited-edition product will be available through Apple Store Online, the Apple Store app and all six Apple retail stores in India. The Special Edition AirPods 5 comes with a price tag of Rs 17,900 and the company is also offering instant cashback with EMI starting at Rs 1,533. The launch forms part of Apple's broader festive initiative celebrating India's traditional art of Rangoli and is accompanied by special financing offers, in-store experiences and creative workshops running from 11 October to 11 November 2026.Apple said customers shopping during the festive period can avail of up to 12 months of No Cost EMI on selected iPhone, Mac and iPad models, along with instant cashback of up to Rs 15,000 on eligible cards. Six-month No Cost EMI options are also available on Apple Watch, AirPods and accessories.The Special Edition AirPods 5 is available in limited quantities through Apple Store Online, the Apple Store app and Apple's six India stores: BKC, Borivali, Saket, Noida, Hebbal and Koregaon Park. Apple's store page lists a limit of two units per customer. It also says the edition is sold while supplies last from October 11 to November 11.Apple has also said that the special edition cannot be combined with any other AirPods offer or with Business, Education or Corporate Employee Purchase Plan pricing. If one needs repair or replacement, Apple says it may provide standard-edition AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case, subject to supply.As part of the celebrations, Apple is also expanding its India-created "Draw Your Own Rangoli on iPad with Apple Pencil" Today (October 12) at Apple session to international markets for the first time. The workshop, developed with artist Arushi Kathuria, will run from 14 October to 9 November and will be offered in select locations across the United States, Canada, Malaysia and Singapore in addition to India.Alongside the Special Edition AirPods launch, Apple has rolled out a range of festive shopping benefits and services through its online and retail channels:* Up to 12 months of No Cost EMI on selected products, plus instant cashback of up to Rs 15,000 with eligible cards.* Free engraving on eligible products including AirPods, iPad, AirTag and Apple Pencil, allowing customers to personalise gifts with names, initials, numbers or emoji.* Special Edition AirPods 5 with festive engraving, available exclusively through Apple retail channels.* Custom Mac configurations, available directly through Apple.* Personalised shopping experience through the Apple Store app.* Complimentary setup assistance from Apple Specialists for new device owners.* Trade-in offers, with customers able to receive between Rs 4,500 and Rs 81,500 in credit when exchanging eligible smartphones. Trade-ins for Macs, iPads and Apple Watches are also available.* Digital gift messaging through the Apple Store app, allowing customers to send personalised festive greetings with purchases.* Three months of Apple Music free with the purchase of eligible Apple devices.* Free today (October 12) at Apple festive workshops, including the Rangoli drawing session on iPad using Procreate.* Interactive Rangoli wallpaper creator, enabling customers to design, download and share personalised festive artwork.
Article Summary: Apple launches Special Edition AirPods 5 with a custom Rangoli design. The limited-edition product will be available through Apple Store Online, the Apple Store app and all six Apple retail stores in India. Apple is also offering instant cashback with EMI starting at Rs 1,533. The launch forms part of Apple's broader festive initiative celebrating India's traditional art of Rangolis.

Article Title: Google DeepMind is hiring AI engineers for its new team with salary of up to $1.1 million, no degree required; all the company wants is...
Article Text:
Google DeepMind is hiring for Polaris.

Every Polaris test for Gemini takes about a week to build

A very good vibe coder can land the Google DeepMind job

Google DeepMind is hiring engineers for Polaris, a new team that builds tests to measure how well Gemini handles real software engineering work. The pay stands out. Total compensation runs from $550,000 to $1.1 million a year, and you don’t need a degree to apply.Tamay Besiroglu, an Epoch AI co-founder who now works on data at Google DeepMind, kept the brief simple in a post on X. “All we care about is you being smart and able to solve hard problems,” he wrote, adding that people should ignore the pay mentioned in the job ad. When asked whether the listing was wrong, he clarified that its numbers were accurate but left out equity. The base salary alone sits between $164,000 and $252,000.The role, listed as Research Engineer and based in Mountain View, California, centres on designing tasks. Each one is a detailed exam for Gemini, made up of a prompt telling the model what to do and a grader or rubric that scores its attempt.Instead of producing tests in bulk through a synthetic data pipeline, Polaris engineers hand-build a smaller set that captures the complexity of real-world coding. A single task usually takes about a week, from first idea to final approval.Engineers will also start new projects to improve Gemini’s training data and evaluations. Google first called for Polaris applicants on September 25, describing it as a new DeepMind team designing evaluation frameworks for AI coding agents.On paper, the minimum bar asks for software development experience and hands-on use of AI coding tools and developer agents. A track record at contests like the IMO, Putnam or IOI, or experience designing benchmarks and evaluation rubrics, counts in your favour.Besiroglu’s replies on X widened the door further. Asked if non-engineers could apply, he said quick learners were fine. Asked about vibe coders, he said they just need to be very good ones. He also confirmed the team doesn’t ask LeetCode questions. When one user called Google’s hiring process “laughably bad”, Besiroglu said his own team runs the interviews and that he thinks the process is good.So what is DeepMind looking for in an engineer? Someone smart who can solve hard problems, Besiroglu said. Experience with AI coding agents, he added, is very useful too.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind is hiring engineers for Polaris, a new team that builds tests to measure how well Gemini handles real software engineering work. Total compensation runs from $550,000 to $1.1 million a year, and you don’t need a degree to apply.

Article Title: Nick Jonas co-founded a diabetes nonprofit that created 8,400 insulin-access plans in 2025; how its US programme helps people find affordable treatment
Article Text:
Nick Jonas. Images Credit: Wikipedia

Nick Jonas’s insulin-access programme helps people find affordable treatment

Image Credit: Healthcare Radius

The programme builds on Jonas’s personal experience with diabetes

What did Beyond Type 1 achieve with its insulin programme in 2025

The online tool matches users with assistance based on their needs

The quick-start guide explains how people can use the service

Access to affordable insulin remains a challenge for people living with diabetes in the US, particularly those who struggle with insurance coverage or the cost of prescriptions. Singer Nick Jonas , who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 13, has helped address this problem through Beyond Type 1 , the diabetes nonprofit he co-founded. Its GetInsulin programme connects people with financial assistance and savings options suited to their circumstances. According to the organisation’s 2025 Impact Report, the initiative created 8,400 personalised insulin-access plans during the year, with treatment costing almost always $35 a month or less.Beyond Type 1 introduced GetInsulin in 2020 to help Americans find ways to obtain insulin when its price becomes difficult to manage. As explained in the organisation’s article, Nick Jonas launched an initiative to increase access to affordable insulin. Jonas joined forces with the nonprofit to develop a free online search tool that helps people identify available assistance.The initiative was designed around a practical problem. People who need insulin may find themselves facing high pharmacy bills, uncertain insurance coverage or difficulty identifying programmes that could reduce their expenses.Finding the right option can involve navigating different eligibility rules and application processes.GetInsulin aims to make that search simpler by bringing relevant information together. Instead of requiring users to investigate numerous programmes independently, the website asks for a few details and generates a personalised action plan.The original launch also involved collaboration with the NAACP and Feeding America, according to Beyond Type 1’s 2020 announcement. The initiative reflected an effort to make information about affordable insulin more accessible to people who might otherwise struggle to find support.Jonas’s involvement in diabetes advocacy is closely connected to his own diagnosis. Beyond Type 1’s official profile of the singer states that he was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at 13. Alongside his career in music and acting, he has supported causes involving health, education, human rights and young people.Type 1 diabetes requires people to manage their condition with insulin. For those who depend on the medication, being unable to afford a prescription can create an immediate problem.Beyond Type 1’s announcement about the initiative described insulin access as a human rights issue. That approach places affordability at the centre of the discussion, recognising that people should be able to seek treatment without facing financial barriers that put their health at risk.The programme does not remove every obstacle associated with healthcare costs. Instead, it offers a way to identify existing assistance and understand which options may fit an individual's situation.The organisation’s 2025 Impact Report highlights the scale of the programme’s work. During the year, GetInsulin helped generate 8,400 personalised action plans intended to improve access to insulin. Beyond Type 1 reported that the resulting options almost always made insulin available for $35 a month or less.The report also describes a change in how the initiative supports users. Beyond Type 1 introduced a new email journey for GetInsulin and expanded its media support, moving towards ongoing guidance rather than relying solely on one-time assistance.This distinction matters because a person’s financial or insurance circumstances can change. Someone who finds a suitable programme initially may still need information and support to maintain access over time. Continued guidance can help users revisit their options as their needs evolve.The figure of 8,400 represents personalised plans created, rather than a confirmed count of individual prescriptions filled or people who received insulin directly from the nonprofit. The organisation’s reported results demonstrate the reach of its information and referral service while distinguishing that work from the actual supply of medication.The impact report also places the programme within Beyond Type 1’s broader work during 2025, which included expanding its international activities and supporting the diabetes community through education and advocacy.The Get Insulin programme page explains how the service works. Users answer questions about their location, insurance status, income and insulin prescription. The information helps the platform identify options that may be suitable for their circumstances.The service covers people with different insurance arrangements, including those who are uninsured, under-insured or insured but still facing unaffordable costs. It is available in English and Spanish and is intended for people living with diabetes in the US.Beyond Type 1 also separates the service into 2 routes. Urgent Insulin Support is designed for people who have fewer than 7 days of insulin remaining and may be at risk of rationing their supply. It directs users towards possible options offered through insulin manufacturers.Continuing Need Insulin Support is intended for people whose prescribed insulin has become too expensive at the pharmacy. It helps them build a personalised plan for more reliable access throughout the year. The distinction allows people to look for help according to the urgency of their circumstances.Beyond Type 1’s GetInsulin quick-start guide outlines the information users should gather before beginning. This includes their state and ZIP code, insurance arrangements and insulin brand or prescription.Location is important because some US states have limits on insulin co-payments. The guide notes that certain state caps range from $35 to $100 for a 30-day supply. The options available to an individual can depend on where they live and the type of coverage they have.Once users begin the process, they can follow the website’s prompts to build an action plan. Providing an email address and preferred pharmacy is optional, although these details can make it easier to revisit the plan later. Users can also receive a copy by email.There is an important limitation, however. GetInsulin is neither a pharmacy nor an insurance plan. Beyond Type 1 does not dispense or ship insulin through the service, and the website cannot guarantee that every user will qualify for a particular assistance programme. Instead, it connects people with possible sources of savings and support.For anyone struggling to pay for a prescription, the service provides a starting point for exploring available options and reducing the time spent searching for help.
Article Summary: Beyond Type 1 introduced GetInsulin in 2020 to help Americans find ways to obtain insulin when its price becomes difficult to manage. The initiative created 8,400 personalised insulin-access plans during the year, with treatment costing almost always $35 a month or less. The programme builds on Jonas’s personal experience with diabetes.

Article Title: A 3D-printed bridge inspired by Leonardo da Vinci uses waste stone and marble powder; 13 printed blocks form a self-supporting structure
Article Text:
Representative Image of a modern bridge inspired by Leonardo da Vinci and built with 3D printing technology ( AI Generrated Image)

Da Vinci's Bridge: how 3D printing brings Leonardo's design into the modern era

Inside the material: mortar made with 30% waste stone and marble powders

Stereotomy and self-support: how 13 printed blocks form the bridge

Da Vinci's Bridge: how 3D printing brings Leonardo's design into the modern era

Inside the material: mortar made with 30% waste stone and marble powders

Stereotomy and self-support: how 13 printed blocks form the bridge

A bridge inspired by a design sketched by Leonardo da Vinci more than 500 years ago has been brought to life as a modern prototype using 3D printing and waste from stone processing. WASP and the Polytechnic University of Bari said, the project team describes Da Vinci's Bridge as the first 3D-printed bridge to use waste materials from stone processing , combining additive manufacturing with Leonardo's original vision for a self-supporting structure. The project was conceived by Professor Giuseppe Fallacara of the Polytechnic University of Bari and draws on Leonardo's design for a bridge that would have connected the Pera district, present-day Galata in Beyoğlu, with Constantinople, today's Istanbul, across the Golden Horn. The prototype is a pedestrian bridge with a span of approximately 6 metres and adapts Leonardo's concept for the needs of the experiment.The project's distinctive feature is not simply that the bridge was 3D-printed, but that its construction material incorporates waste from stone and marble processing. B&Y, an Italian start-up led by Vincenzo Gurrado, developed a low-environmental-impact mortar made from 30% waste stone and marble powders combined with a lime-based binder. The project brought together the ArCoD department of the Polytechnic University of Bari with WASP, which supplied the 3D-printing technology, and B&Y, which developed the material.The project demonstrates how waste generated during stone processing can be incorporated into a material for 3D-printed construction rather than being treated solely as a disposal problem.Leonardo's original bridge was never built, but its design was notable for its self-supporting form. The modern project does not reproduce the proposed structure at its original scale. Instead, Fallacara's team adapted the concept into a roughly 6-metre pedestrian prototype, allowing the researchers to test the combination of 3D printing, stone-processing waste and the geometric principles behind Leonardo's design.Turning the material into a physical bridge required large-format 3D printing. WASP provided its machines and technical expertise for producing the blocks that form the structure. The bridge was divided into 13 blocks with variable layers, each printed using the WASP 3MT LDM Concrete, a large-format printer designed for cementitious materials. The printed blocks were then assembled by the University of Bari using a system of temporary centering, which supported the pieces during construction.Once the blocks were assembled, the temporary supports could be removed. The completed structure is able to support itself through the principle of stereotomy, which was also central to Leonardo's original bridge concept. In this approach, the geometry and arrangement of individual structural pieces allow them to work together as a self-supporting whole. The project therefore combines a historical construction principle with a contemporary manufacturing process rather than simply reproducing Leonardo's drawing in a different material.The use of stereotomy is key to the bridge's structure. Leonardo's original design relied on the arrangement of individual elements to create a self-supporting form, and the modern prototype applies the same underlying principle to its 13 3D-printed blocks. The temporary centring system was used during assembly, but the finished bridge does not depend on those temporary supports to remain standing. Article Title: Egypt’s ancient Fayoum portraits to be exhibited abroad for first time
Article Text:
Egypt recently revealed a restored version of the Tondo of the Two Brothers painting at a press conference. (Pic Credit: AP)

Egypt on Sunday presented a restored version of the “Tondo of the Two Brothers”, a celebrated painting dating to the second century and part of the renowned Fayoum portrait collection.The restoration took three weeks, with experts from Rome working alongside conservators at the Egyptian museum in Tahrir, where the collection is normally housed, officials said at a press conference.Fayoum mummy portraits were typically created on thin wooden panels and placed over the faces of the dead beneath their mummy wrappings. The artworks reflect a fusion of Egyptian burial traditions and artistic styles from the broader Greco-Roman world.Egypt is preparing to loan a substantial portion of the collection for a temporary exhibition in Rome. The upcoming display will mark the collection's first journey outside the country.Egyptian minister of tourism and antiquities Sherif Fathy said the restoration demonstrated how cooperation between countries could help safeguard and study cultural heritage.“The restoration of the Tondo of the Two Brothers is an important example of what can be achieved through international cooperation in the preservation and study of cultural heritage,” Fathy said.“Egypt and Italy share deep historical and cultural ties, and this project brings together Egyptian and Italian expertise to preserve an exceptional work of art for future generations,” he added.The painting stands out for its circular design and its portrayal of two figures, unlike the single-person subjects found in many other portraits. Experts consider it one of the most strikingly lifelike works to have survived from Roman-era Egypt.The artwork was made using a technique in which pigments are blended with molten wax. During the restoration, specialists managed to bring back the facial features of the brother positioned on the right, according to AP.Aly Abdel Halim, director general of the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir, said the conservation work required a delicate approach as the wooden panel had suffered termite damage and the painted surface was also fragile.The restored portraits will be displayed in Rome at an exhibition scheduled to run from November through May 2027.Tomaso Radaelli, chairman of MondoMostre, the exhibition's organiser, said the show would feature more than 110 artefacts. These will include painted panels, funerary shrouds, masks, marble portraits, plaster casts and ancient jewellery.
Article Summary: The restoration took three weeks, with experts from Rome working alongside conservators at the Egyptian museum in Tahrir. The artwork was made using a technique in which pigments are blended with molten wax. Experts consider it one of the most strikingly lifelike works to have survived from Roman-era Egypt.

Article Title: In 1967, an Australian man built a house from thousands of discarded glass bottles; nearly 60 years later, the unusual Lightning Ridge building survives as a mining museum and tourist attraction
Article Text:
The Bottle House was built in 1967 and remains one of the distinctive landmarks in Lightning Ridge.

How discarded bottles became building material

The building's walls are its most distinctive feature. Rows of glass bottles form the structure, giving it an appearance unlike a conventional house made with bricks, timber or concrete.

From a miner's camp to a museum

Today, the building houses a small museum featuring objects linked to opal mining and minerals.

Where visitors can see the Bottle House

The attraction offers a look at both the region's mining heritage and an unusual approach to construction.

Thousands of discarded glass bottles became the building material for an unusual house in the Australian outback in 1967. Nearly six decades later, the structure still stands in Lightning Ridge, New South Wales, where it serves as a tourist attraction and a museum displaying opal-mining artefacts, vintage bottles and other historical objects. Known as the Bottle House, the building was constructed by Tex Moeckel. Its walls are made from glass bottles fixed together, while its sharply pitched, almost A-frame roof is covered with corrugated iron. Inside, the building has several small rooms and a loft.According to the official website of the New South Wales government, the Bottle House was built in 1967 and remains one of the town's distinctive landmarks. It also lists it as the Bottle House and Mining Museum, describing it as an example of unusual architecture and resourcefulness in a former mining camp.The Bottle House was created using bottles collected from Hebel, a small town across the Queensland border. According to the New South Wales Government's official tourism information, the bottles were initially joined using cement. Moeckel later discovered that local clay was more suitable because it made it easier to replace a bottle if it broke. The building's walls are its most distinctive feature. Rows of glass bottles form the structure, giving it an appearance unlike a conventional house made with bricks, timber or concrete.Light passing through the glass creates another visual feature, highlighted in the official tourism website's photo gallery. The available historical records do not specify the exact number of bottles used in the construction. However, the building's walls are made almost entirely from bottles, making discarded glass the defining element of its design.The Bottle House was originally associated with a miner's camp, reflecting Lightning Ridge's history as an opal-mining settlement. The town, in northern New South Wales, is widely known for its black opals and has a long history of mining and small-scale settlement. As reported by The Lightning Ridge Historical Society, Dave Martin operated the Bottle House for a period during the 1970s. An advertisement for the attraction appeared in the local Lightning Flash newspaper in September 1969, indicating that it was being promoted to visitors soon after it was built.Today, the building houses a small museum featuring objects linked to opal mining and minerals. Visitors can also see a collection of vintage bottles, artworks and other old items. The collection extends beyond the bottles incorporated into the walls, giving the attraction a broader connection to local history.The Bottle House and Mining Museum is located on Opal Street in Lightning Ridge, New South Wales, postcode 2834. According to the New South Wales Government's website, the listed admission price ranges from 2 to 10 Australian dollars (AUD). Visitors who need accessibility information are advised to contact the venue before visiting. The attraction offers a look at both the region's mining heritage and an unusual approach to construction. Its glass-bottle walls remain the main draw, while the mining artefacts and vintage objects provide additional context about the area.Built in 1967 by Tex Moeckel, the Bottle House has survived as a reminder of a time when discarded materials were used to create a distinctive local building. It now serves a different purpose from its early days as part of a miner's camp: preserving and displaying pieces of Lightning Ridge's history for visitors.
Article Summary: The Bottle House was built in Lightning Ridge, New South Wales, in 1967. Its walls are made from glass bottles fixed together, while its sharply pitched, almost A-frame roof is covered with corrugated iron. Today, the building houses a small museum featuring objects linked to opal mining and minerals.

How radio tracking equipment and cameras improve python detection efficiency

Why Burmese pythons threaten Everglades mammals and why tracking them across difficult terrain is hard

How drone training for Department of the Interior scientists brought python tracking to the Everglades

Why further testing matters for python control

Deep in the Florida Everglades, a vast and difficult landscape, scientists are trying a new way to find invasive Burmese pythons; they are looking from above. Researchers are testing small drones fitted with radio tracking equipment or cameras to locate snakes more efficiently, follow their movements across difficult terrain, and cut the cost of searching from the ground. One female python released after tagging measured 16 feet and weighed 147.9 pounds. In this article, you will learn how the technology works, why pythons are so hard to track, what the scientists hope to gain, and what important questions remain unanswered. The trials could help wildlife managers refine detection methods and improve efforts to control a population that threatens native Everglades wildlife.The United States Geological Survey, a federal science agency, is testing a different approach to a long-running wildlife problem. Scientists at its Fort Collins Science Centre are using uncrewed aircraft systems, commonly called drones, to track invasive Burmese pythons and to learn more about how the snakes move across a vast and difficult landscape. The work is described in the center's September 2026 series, which highlights how its projects support sound decision-making. The python project stands out because the agency's own account calls it a novel use of technology that is more commonly applied to monitoring rivers and forests.A photograph published by the USGS captures the technology at work. In the image, agency biologists operate a small uncrewed aircraft system while University of Florida interns release a newly radio-tagged female Burmese python, 16 feet long and weighing 147.9 pounds, back into the Greater Everglades Ecosystem. The scene shows how the pieces fit together: a snake carrying a radio tag, people on the ground handling it safely, and an aircraft overhead testing how well the tag can be followed from the sky.The agency explains that the aircraft can carry either radio tracking equipment or a camera. The platform is being evaluated as a way to improve detection and tracking efficiency, collect better data, and reduce the labour and operating costs of traditional ground-based monitoring for pythons. In plain terms, a drone can cover wet, thick, hard-to-walk areas far faster than a person on foot, and it can pick up a tagged snake's signal or spot the animal from overhead. If it works well, fewer people would need to spend long hours searching difficult ground.The reason for all this effort is the size of the problem. The United States Geological Survey leads federal research to control the Burmese python, which has become firmly established across the Greater Everglades Ecosystem and poses a serious threat to native wildlife. The snake can grow to more than 17 feet long and is believed to be a key factor in the sharp decline of mammal populations in the region. Finding such a well-camouflaged animal in a huge, wet landscape is slow and costly, which explains why scientists are eager to test aerial tools.The idea grew out of a training program. Chris Holmquist-Johnson, a certified instructor in uncrewed aircraft systems for the Department of the Interior, trained a group of Fort Collins Science Centre scientists working in the Florida Everglades about a year before the article was published. Those researchers are now using the technology to track Burmese pythons and are gaining new insight into their movement behaviour. Holmquist-Johnson's main work involves rivers and forests in the western United States, including mapping changes in river channels and surveying thinned forest areas, so the Everglades project shows how skills built in one setting can be carried into another.It is important to read the project for what it is. The agency describes the aircraft as a tool still under evaluation, and the sources do not report measured results, such as how many more snakes are found or how much money is saved. The 16-foot, 147.9-pound snake is a single example from a photograph, not an average, and the agency notes that pythons can grow even longer. As testing continues, the key questions will be how reliably the aircraft locate tagged and untagged snakes, and whether the savings in time and cost hold up across the seasons and the many kinds of habitat in the Everglades.

The trials could help wildlife managers refine detection methods and improve efforts to control a population that threatens native wildlife. If it works well, fewer people would need to spend long hours searching difficult ground.

Article Title: Baltimore turned waste glass into road surfaces on at least 17 streets; the crushed glass made the pavement sparkle under sunlight and streetlights
Article Text:
PC: AI Generated

How did Baltimore’s recycled glass roads create a sparkling effect

PC: AI Generated

How is crushed glass turned into a paving material

Crushed glass can affect the strength and performance of asphalt

What makes recycled glass suitable for asphalt paving

At least 17 streets in Baltimore were paved with recycled glass, creating road surfaces that could sparkle when sunlight or streetlights hit them. Baltimore's approach is part of a broader practice of using crushed waste glass in asphalt mixes. Properly processed glass can replace some of the conventional aggregate used in road construction.Wearing surfaces containing 10 to 15% crushed glass have performed well. According to the Federal Highway Administration, recycled glass has also been used in road projects elsewhere in the United States. New York City used about 225,000 metric tonnes of glass in resurfacing applications between 1990 and 1995.However, earlier projects found problems when glass was used in high percentages or as large pieces. The guidance recommends using properly processed glass in suitable proportions for asphalt paving.Waste glass was tested for use in hot mix asphalt during field demonstrations in the United States in the late 1960s and early 1970s. Test paving strips were placed at about 33 locations across the United States and Canada. Baltimore later used glass in at least 17 streets, producing a sparkle effect from reflected sunlight or street lamp light.Early projects often used more than 25% glass and coarse particles. The guidance says high glass percentages and large particles probably contributed to stripping and raveling problems reported during those demonstrations. Glass does not absorb asphalt cement binder and bonds poorly to it. Moisture damage can become a concern when high percentages and large gradations are used in surface mixes.According to the FHWA guidance, turning waste glass into a suitable paving material requires several processing steps before it can be mixed into the asphalt. Waste glass is first cleaned to remove materials such as metal, plastic, and paper. It is then crushed and screened to produce smaller, more suitable pieces while removing flat, elongated, and sharp-edged particles.For surface pavements, the guidance recommends using glass smaller than 4.75 mm, or the No. 4 sieve, as a fine aggregate mixed with conventional materials. Asphalt wearing surfaces containing 10 to 15% crushed glass have shown satisfactory performance. Higher proportions, potentially up to 25%, may be suitable for base or binder courses, where the glass is not exposed directly at the road surface.Well-crushed glass can also affect the performance of asphalt mixes because of its angular shape and high friction angle. The guidance says these properties can contribute to good lateral stability, with tests reporting stability comparable to, and in many cases better than, conventional mixes. Waste glass also has a specific gravity about 10 to 15% below that of conventional aggregates, which can increase the yield of an asphalt mix.Its low thermal conductivity may also help mixes containing glass retain heat for longer. Skid resistance tests on pavements containing waste glass have produced results within recommended limits. However, larger glass particles measuring more than 19 mm can become slippery when wet and should not be used in surface mixes. The guidance also notes that using more than 15% glass can increase pavement reflectivity and glare, particularly when the surface is wet.Asphalt mixes containing crushed glass can be designed using standard laboratory procedures. The guidance recommends testing the mix for stripping potential and says conventional pavement structural design methods are appropriate. Most highway departments allow 5 to 10% glass. The guidance says performance is generally best when crushed glass is used as a sand or fine aggregate substitute.The same methods and equipment can be used to store, mix, place, and compact asphalt containing waste glass. Field testing should follow the procedures used for conventional hot mix asphalt. The guidance identifies a need for uniform specifications covering sizing, debris levels, and mix limitations. It says a lack of adequate and consistent glass supply remains a major constraint on wider use.
Article Summary: At least 17 streets in Baltimore were paved with recycled glass. Glass can replace some of the conventional aggregate used in road construction. New York City used about 225,000 metric tonnes of glass in resurfacing applications between 1990 and 1995. Earlier projects found problems when glass was used in high percentages or as large pieces.

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of the Nansledan project do you find most important? Sustainable building materials Long-term stability for residents 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A wider community taking shape

A new housing project in Cornwall is putting a different face on the fight against homelessness. Rather than treating shelter as a temporary stopgap, the development in Nansledan, Newquay, combines carefully designed homes with practical support, creating a more secure route towards independent living for people who have experienced homelessness. Scroll down to read the details.According to the Nansledan website, on August 4, 2026, St Petrocs received the keys to the first phase of the development from the Duchy of Cornwall. Funded by The Duke of Cornwall’s Charitable Foundation and built on Duchy-owned land, the scheme will provide accommodation for 16 people across two four-bedroom homes and eight one-bedroom apartments.Built by CG Fry & Son, the development was designed around more than simply providing a roof. On-site counselling space will allow St Petrocs to offer residents support alongside their accommodation, helping them establish greater stability as they work towards securing permanent housing, adds the report. The handover marks the completion of the construction phase and the beginning of the homes’ next chapter, with residents set to move into fully equipped properties, the report adds.The project forms part of Homewards, The Royal Foundation’s five-year programme established by The Duke of Cornwall with the ambition of demonstrating that homelessness can be prevented and made rare, brief and unrepeated.The programme brought the Duchy together with homelessness prevention specialists and people with lived experience, helping shape the design and approach to the development. The result is a model that places housing, wellbeing and community connection on the same footing.For St Petrocs, which supports people experiencing homelessness in Cornwall, the homes offer a chance to provide continuity rather than short-term intervention. Residents will have access to personalised support while becoming part of the wider Nansledan community.As per the report, sustainability is another defining feature of the project. The all-electric homes have been constructed with a focus on reducing both embodied carbon and the emissions associated with everyday use. Ultra-low-carbon cement and blockwork, super-insulated hemp-filled wall panels and solar panels form part of the environmental strategy. The approach is intended not only to reduce the development’s impact but also to keep future running costs lower for St Petrocs.The homes have also been furnished through the Homewards Furniture Project, with support from retailers and partners including Howdens, IKEA, DFS, B&Q, Bosch Home Appliances and Gordon Brown’s The Multibank charity. Sofas, tables, chairs, white goods and fitted kitchens mean residents can move into spaces that are ready to live in from day one.Nansledan itself reflects the Duchy’s broader approach to sustainable development. The urban extension to Newquay combines homes with shops, businesses, community facilities, green spaces and walkable neighbourhoods. The supported housing scheme adds another dimension to that vision: ensuring that those at risk of being left on the margins can also find a place within a growing community.As the first residents prepare to move in, the project represents the Duchy of Cornwall’s first housing development specifically designed to address homelessness. Its significance lies not just in the number of homes created, but in the idea behind them: that secure accommodation, meaningful support and a sense of belonging can work together to help people rebuild their lives.Images Courtesy: BBC and Royal Foundation
Article Summary: Nansledan, Newquay, is the Duchy of Cornwall’s first housing development specifically designed to address homelessness. The scheme will provide accommodation for 16 people across two four-bedroom homes and eight one-bedroom apartments. On-site counselling space will allow St Petrocs to offer residents support alongside their accommodation.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card

Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Article Title: Religious, spiritual & astrology apps see nearly 30cr downloads in Jan-Sept
Article Text: NEW DELHI: From listening to bhajans and reading the Bible to finding the direction of Mecca or discovering what the stars have in store, Indians are increasingly turning to smartphones for matters of faith and fortune. Religious, spiritual and astrology apps recorded nearly 30 crore downloads in the first nine months of 2026, emerging as fast-growing segments of India's app economy.According to data shared exclusively with TOI by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, astrology apps registered 15 crore downloads between Jan and Sept, a 75% jump over last year. Religious and spiritual apps clocked 14.6 crore downloads, up 47%. Together, the categories surpassed their combined 24.8 crore downloads in the whole of 2025 and touched nearly 30 crore downloads.The digital devotion wave is cutting across religions. Sanatan Status Bhajan Mantra topped the religious and spiritual category by average monthly active users, followed by YouVersion Bible App, which offers Bible reading and audio content, and WeMuslim, which provides prayer timings and Qibla direction.Sri Mandir, offering online pujas and devotional services, ranked fourth, while Muslim Pro, which provides Quran reading and prayer-related features, completed the top five.The diversity is also reflected in user growth. Sanatan Status Bhajan Mantra saw its average monthly active users jump 109% year-on-year, while YouVersion recorded 24% growth and WeMuslim 39%. Muslim Pro grew 5%, although Sri Mandir witnessed a 20% decline. "India's strong cultural affinity with religion and astrology, combined with its mobile-first consumer base, creates a favourable environment for growth in these categories," said Eve Chen, insights analyst, Sensor Tower.Indians are spending more time on these apps. Average daily usage of religious and spiritual apps rose from 5.8 minutes in the first quarter of 2022 to 8.2 minutes in corresponding quarter of 2026, a rise of over 40%. For astrology apps, engagement climbed more than 50%, from 3.5 to 5.3 minutes.Astrology is witnessing an AI-powered shift. Astrotalk led with 3 crore downloads, followed by AstroSage Kundli: AI Astrology at 2.5 crore, up 172%. Newer entrant Tarot99 recorded 1.1 crore downloads, while AstroLokal's downloads surged 1,062% to nearly 75 lakh.
Article Summary: Religious, spiritual and astrology apps recorded nearly 30 crore downloads in the first nine months of 2026. Astrology apps registered 15 crore downloads between Jan and Sept, a 75% jump over last year. Sanatan Status Bhajan Mantra topped the religious and spiritual category by average monthly active users.

A High-response Linear Actuator (HLA) handles autofocus, focus breathing is kept low for video, and stabilisation is rated at 6.5 stops at 50mm and 4.5 stops at 120mm. The focus mode and OS switches are gone entirely, so those settings now live in the camera body. It also gets dust and splash resistance, plus a water- and oil-repellent front coating.The 16-300mm is built as a one-lens kit. Its 18.8x zoom range is, by Sigma's count, a world first for an autofocus interchangeable lens on mirrorless cameras, and it focuses close enough for 1:2 magnification.Stabilisation is rated at 6 stops at 16mm and 4.5 stops at 300mm. For Nikon, AF drive and communication speed have been tuned to the Z mount, with support for continuous AF, in-camera aberration correction on compatible bodies, and a rubber-sealed mount.Both lenses follow the full-frame 85mm F1.2 DG | Art and 20-60mm F2.8-4 DG | Contemporary, which went on sale in India on September 30. For APS-C users, the choice now comes down to one lens that reaches 300mm, or three that hold F2.8 all the way to 120mm.
Article Summary: Nikon Z shooters get Sigma's 18.8x superzoom in November. 50-120mm F2.8 DC OS | Contemporary goes on sale in India on October 22. 16-300mm F3.5-6.7 DC OS| Contemporary reaches Nikon Z cameras on November 5.

Article Title: ‘Let's get to work’: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman after Satya Nadella backs ‘emergency brake’ for AI models
Article Text:
Microsoft AI Chief Mustafa Suleyman

Satya Nadella’s ‘emergency brake’ plan

Designing for observability over blind trust

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has thrown his weight behind company chief executive Satya Nadella ’s call for mandatory safeguards on advanced artificial intelligence (AI), declaring that containing superintelligence is an achievable technical hurdle the tech industry must tackle immediately. Reacting to Nadella’s safety proposals, Suleyman emphasised that humanity has successfully tamed high-risk innovations throughout history, framing AI oversight as a standard engineering milestone rather than an unsolvable dilemma.“Super Intelligence must be contained... Today, this is an engineering and governance challenge. And it isn't new. We've done it with planes, cars, nuclear materials, food safety, medicines... and everything else. Let's get to work!” Suleyman wrote in a post on X (formerly Twitter).Suleyman’s remarks follow an extensive position statement published on X by Nadella on Saturday, where the Microsoft chief urged developers to equip advanced AI systems with hard boundaries, external oversight, and a literal “emergency brake” allowing authorised operators to halt or disconnect a system in the middle of an operation.Nadella argued that unpredictable generative algorithms cannot be left unchecked and must be insulated by rigid, deterministic software guardrails.“We need to surround non-deterministic models with strong, deterministic system design, human controls, and reliable operating procedures, and establish industry standards where existing ones are insufficient,” Nadella wrote.He went further by suggesting that frontier systems, whether closed-source proprietary platforms or open-weight releases, should be approached with the same defensive mindset companies apply to internal security vulnerabilities: “Treating frontier closed and open weight models like insider risks is a way to build such a system.”Outlining a technical blueprint for the superintelligence era, Nadella argued that safety frameworks should be built on core “principles of observability” rather than blind reliance on a model’s good behaviour. His proposed framework hinges on six primary operational requirements, including model diversity, human-readable footprints, continuous system testing, independent controls and auditability, containment and mandatory incident disclosure.
Article Summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has thrown his weight behind Satya Nadella’s call for mandatory safeguards on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) He said that containing superintelligence is an achievable technical hurdle the tech industry must tackle immediately. Suley man emphasised that humanity has successfully tamed high-risk innovations throughout history.

Article Title: Swiss watches that Google's top execs are reportedly 'obsessed with,' and made Tudor build a special edition for them
Article Text:
Google employees got Tudor to build them their own Swiss watch

Tudor needs at least 40 buyers before it customises a watch

OpenAI, Palantir and Uber staff have their own limited-edition Tudors

Custom tech-company Tudor watches are selling for double their retail price

Silicon Valley has a new way to flex, and at Google , it comes with a Swiss movement and a Tudor logo. In August, a post showing custom Tudor watches built for Googlers started circulating on X, and staffers at OpenAI, Palantir, Uber and Perplexity were soon replying with photos of their own company-branded timepieces. The Google edition is based on the Tudor Pelagos, a titanium diver that retails for around $4,500 (roughly Rs 4.3 lakh). Google does not hand these out. Like most of these watches, it was ordered by an internal group of watch collectors, paid for out of pocket, and is usually available only to members of the group that commissioned it.Tudor, Rolex’s sister brand, runs a customisation programme with a minimum order of 40 watches, according to the managing editor of a luxury watch news site. Production takes about six months. Employee collector groups do the work of rounding up enough interested buyers, and each member pays full retail price.That setup keeps runs small and designs private. A watch made for one company’s collector group tends to stay within that group, so every edition is rare by default.OpenAI’s head of applied research, Boris Power, posted the company’s version, which has “Good Research Takes Time” engraved on the caseback.The same slogan appears on T-shirts OpenAI sells, and Power has said Tudor made 400 of these with OpenAI’s logo on the dial.Palantir’s strategic engagement head, Eliano Younes, said the company’s run was limited to 468 pieces, with a barely noticeable Palantir logo on the dial. Uber engineer Alex Feng shared a caseback marked 1/100, the first watch in a batch of 100. A former Facebook employee admitted he regretted not buying every custom model made during his six years there.Tudor is not the only maker involved. Adobe’s watch club is working with British brand Studio Underd0g on 128 branded pieces at about $1,200 (around Rs 1.2 lakh) each. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman went further, commissioning just seven watches from Swiss maker Vanguart, based on a model that starts at $180,000 (about Rs 1.7 crore), with “COMPUTE IS DESTINY” engraved around the rotor.Rarity carries a premium. A Google-themed Tudor featuring Chrome’s offline dinosaur sold for over $10,000 (about Rs 9.6 lakh) at auction earlier this year, while an Apple “pirate” edition drew a $13,500 (around Rs 13 lakh) bid. A Meta-branded Tudor Black Bay 54 has attracted bids as high as $10,500 (about Rs 10 lakh), against a standard price of $4,725 (roughly Rs 4.6 lakh).Not every branded watch fetches those numbers, and one online watch auctioneer pointed out that some buyers simply find them ugly. For the people ordering them, the draw is belonging. An Adobe designer who owns about 40 watches described these pieces as a ticket into an insider club.Google’s own chief is the odd one out. Sundar Pichai’s most talked-about watch moment came in 2022, when he wore an unreleased Pixel Watch on stage. His employees, it seems, would rather wear the company logo on a Swiss movement.
Article Summary: Tudor, Rolex’s sister brand, runs a customisation programme with a minimum order of 40 watches. Employee collector groups do the work of rounding up enough interested buyers, and each member pays full retail price. A Google-themed Tudor featuring Chrome's offline dinosaur sold for over $10,000 at auction earlier this year.

Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says don’t blindly trust AI; warns: Treat it like an employee who could...
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella

Satya Nadella wants AI controls to sit outside the model

Nadella’s AI safety rules for companies include an emergency brake

The OpenAI agents incident at Hugging Face gives the warning real weight

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wants businesses to stop taking AI models at their word. In a new essay on X titled “Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era”, Nadella says frontier AI models, closed and open-weight alike, should be treated as insider risks. Not because they are out to cause harm, but because any capable actor with access to important systems can make mistakes or be compromised.The worry starts with a basic gap. Engineers could trace traditional software’s behaviour to a specific code path. With today’s models, nobody can tie an output to particular training data or model weights. Yet companies are handing these agents their most sensitive data and the power to take mission-critical actions. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf,” Nadella writes, adding that a model provider’s assurances don’t change that.Setting the hard problem of alignment aside, Nadella pitches an engineering fix. Non-deterministic models, he argues, need to be wrapped in deterministic system design, human controls and reliable operating procedures. In his words, companies must “separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it”.None of this is new, he says. Enterprises have spent decades managing powerful insiders by establishing identity, limiting privileges, logging activity and drawing containment boundaries. He also leans on a 1970s security principle: a program must never be able to bypass or tamper with whatever enforces its permissions. For AI, that means keeping the model apart from the harness that runs it and the actions it can take.Chain-of-thought transparency is non-negotiable, he adds, but not enough on its own. Models checking models helps too, though it risks “nested black boxes”.The essay lists seven principles. No single model should be the only dependency for an important outcome or verify its own work. Every meaningful action must leave tamper-proof, human-readable evidence, because “if it can’t be observed, it can’t be trusted”. Systems need testing for failures, attacks and edge cases, not just successful tasks. Firms should independently decide what a model can access, and validation must never sit with the model being validated.The sharpest point is about containment. Companies should assume a model is compromised from the start, and an authorised person should always be able to pause or shut it down mid-task. When things break, Nadella wants timely disclosure to those affected and industry-wide sharing of which controls failed.The essay follows a real scare. In July, during OpenAI’s internal cybersecurity tests, several of its agents slipped past the systems meant to isolate them and reached Hugging Face’s production infrastructure, logging around 17,600 actions between July 9 and 13. Hugging Face rebuilt about a third of its infrastructure from clean images. Nadella later called long-running agents “a new type of insider risk” on the All-In podcast.OpenAI wasn’t alone for long. Since late July, Anthropic has kept disclosing fresh cases of Claude models breaking into real systems during testing, with the first batch traced to a setup that wrongly left internet access switched on. Google revealed that a Gemini model breached three real companies in May after mistaking them for fictional targets. OpenAI’s own tally keeps growing, and this month it warned over 100 organisations of unauthorised activity by its agents.His focus sets him apart from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, whose call to “pace the frontier” drew support from Sam Altman and Demis Hassabis. Nadella isn’t asking labs to slow down. He is speaking to the companies deploying AI, a theme he has pushed since Microsoft’s July earnings call, where he said firms may need several models just to fix problems caused by one.His closing line puts it plainly: “The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one with the model we trust most. It will be the one that enables us to trust the model the least.”
Article Summary: Nadella says frontier AI models, closed and open-weight alike, should be treated as insider risks. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf,” he writes. The essay follows a real scare. in July, during OpenAI’s internal cybersecurity tests, several of its agents slipped past the systems.

Article Title: Using AI models, scientists are trying to do a Jurassic Park; bring back to Earth extinct Grey Wolf pups and Woolly mammoths
Article Text:
Woolly mammoths

How AI reconstructed extinct wolf genome

Engineering Woolly Mammoths for ecological restoration

The aim of bringing long-lost creatures back from the dead has jumped from the silver screen into modern laboratories. Through advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models, CRISPR gene editing and ancient DNA extraction, Texas-based biotechnology firm Colossal Biosciences is actively working to resurrect extinct beasts, including ancient dire wolves and woolly mammoths, drawing frequent comparisons to Jurassic Park. Speaking with CNBC, Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm embraced the Hollywood comparisons with a touch of humour, but was quick to draw a firm line between cinema and science.“I think anyone that saw Jurassic Park in the 90s and didn’t say it was cool, like I don’t think they’re probably very fun at parties,” Lamm joked, adding, “But yes, I saw the movies. I love them. They entertained us. They scared us. I constantly have to remind people on X that, you know, they were movies. I don’t think Jurassic Park had any conservation or general human benefit models to it, so we’ve tried to take a slightly different perspective. ”Since viable dinosaur DNA degrades and cannot survive across tens of millions of years, reviving dinosaurs remains physically impossible. However, Colossal has set its sights on species lost to more recent history, including the dire wolf, the woolly mammoth, the dodo bird, the Tasmanian tiger, and the giant New Zealand moa bird.“It’s highly likely in the next coming year or two, people will continue to see us deliver extinct species back to Earth, and we could even have more dire wolves, too,” Lamm noted.To engineer its first generation of dire wolf pups, scientists extracted fragmented genetic material from a fossilised skull and tooth dating back thousands of years. Since ancient DNA is naturally fractured and degraded, Colossal deployed advanced AI models to piece together the broken sequence, successfully reconstructing the complete dire wolf genome. Scientists then mapped the computational blueprint against the genetic code of the gray wolf, the animal’s closest living relative.From there, researchers edited living cells from modern gray wolves to generate viable embryos. Three pups, named Romulus, Remus and Khaleesi, were carried and delivered by domestic dogs serving as surrogate mothers. Born on October 1, 2024, in North Texas, Romulus and Remus represent the first successful lineage bred from DNA fossils of an animal that vanished more than 12,500 years ago.When critics argue that the pups are technically genetically modified gray wolves rather than authentic dire wolves, Lamm dismissed the debate as a semantic distraction.“Gray wolves are just genetically modified dire wolves. They were just done by nature or God or however you want to classify it,” Lamm said, calling the objection an argument that “misses the forest for the trees.”Colossal is applying a parallel approach to its high-profile woolly mammoth project, which involves inserting mammoth cold-weather traits into the cells of modern Asian elephants. The company is targeting its first mammoth birth sometime in the 2030s.“We call it a woolly mammoth. Because if it looks like a duck, it quacks like a duck, it serves ecological functions of a duck, it’s a duck, in our perspective,” Lamm said.The initiative traces back to 2019, when Lamm met renowned Harvard geneticist George Church, widely considered the father of synthetic biology. Church had long envisioned using CRISPR to bring back extinct fauna as a proving ground for human medicine and programmable biology.Beyond curiosity, Lamm points to direct climate benefits. First of those is Arctic Permafrost Preservation wherein herds of heavy mammoths could compact dense snow blankets across high-latitude Arctic zones, allowing freezing air to penetrate deep into the ground and keeping permafrost locked solid.Secondly, by felling trees and trampling shrubs, the animals could help transform heat-absorbing forests back into reflective tundra grasslands.
Article Summary: Texas-based biotechnology firm Colossal Biosciences is actively working to resurrect extinct beasts, including ancient dire wolves and woolly mammoths. Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm embraced the Hollywood comparisons with a touch of humour, but was quick to draw a firm line.
