Article Title: Solar farms in France restored native wildflowers and proved beneficial for bees and butterflies, proving to scientists what everyone believed wrong, not all pollinating plants kill insects or ...
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

“inter-row”

Shade changes the way plants and insects interact

“microclimates”

“a physical barrier”

Solar farms could still benefit native plants

“pollinator-friendly”

“net loss of pollinator biodiversity.”

French solar farms are bringing back native wildflowers. The findings also showed that these sites can support bees and butterflies, challenging the notion that solar farms uniformly harm pollinating insects and the plants they depend on. Solar farms produce clean energy, but the panels reshape the surrounding landscape. Those changes can include shifts in temperature, moisture, and vegetation, and research shows solar sites can encourage native plant growth. But the panels can also create shaded areas that affect plant-pollinator interactions.An article in the journal Biological Conservation examined the effects of solar panels on plant-pollinator interactions at 20 solar farms in Southern France. The study found that plants under the panels had 76-86% fewer pollinator visits than plants outside them. But the impact varied across the farm.Researchers found thatplants, which grow between rows of solar panels, continued to attract bees, butterflies and other pollinators. Their numbers were lower than in areas outside the solar farms, but the difference was less pronounced than in areas under constant shade.The researchers found that much of this variation was linked to how much shade the panels cast. Plants in continuous shade attracted fewer visits, but plants in partial shade between rows of panels still attracted pollinators. We found more pollinator activity in the sunnier spots.The researchers suspect the pattern may be partly due to the cooler conditions produced by solar panels. Pollinators tend to avoid cooler and shaded areas, creating what the study calls differentaround the panels.Shade can also affect the plants themselves. Reduced sunlight can decrease plant diversity and the quantity of pollen and nectar flowers produce. This means that even when pollinators do visit plants growing under panels, these plants may provide fewer resources.The research also examines whether the panels themselves may affect insect movement. The research suggests that solar installations may serve asfor butterflies that respond strongly to changes in their environment. Changes in soil moisture under the solar panels may also affect plant growth and insect feeding.The findings do not mean solar farms are inherently harmful to pollinators. Instead, they show that conditions within the same solar installation can vary depending on panel placement, vegetation and land management.The researchers also discovered something unexpected about land maintenance. Grazing led to lower pollinator abundance than mowing, the opposite of what the scientists expected.As Europe continues expanding solar power, researchers want future studies to examine pollinator behaviour in greater detail, including differences between individual species. More data could help scientists understand how solar panels alter local microclimates and how those changes affect pollination.The broader question is how solar farms can be designed and managed to becomewhile avoiding aThe French study suggests that solar installations can alter pollinator activity, but it also shows that their effects are not uniform, leaving room to explore how native vegetation and better land management could make these energy sites more compatible with bees, butterflies and other insects.
Article Summary: Solar farms produce clean energy, but the panels reshape the surrounding landscape. Research shows solar sites can encourage native plant growth. But the panels can also create shaded areas that affect plant-pollinator interactions. The French study suggests that solar installations can alter pollinator activity, but it also shows that their effects are not uniform.

Article Title: Explained: Xbox XP, company’s plan to expand gaming franchises into film, TV and theme parks
Article Text:
Xbox XP : New appointments

Xbox XP: The four core pillars

Xbox pictures : Adapting game lore and characters into television shows, feature films, and linear media to engage wider audiences.

: Adapting game lore and characters into television shows, feature films, and linear media to engage wider audiences. Xbox products : Designing and manufacturing authentic merchandise that allows fans to celebrate their favorite gaming universes.

: Designing and manufacturing authentic merchandise that allows fans to celebrate their favorite gaming universes. Xbox places : Engineering real-world interactions, including physical attractions, themed destinations, live events, broadcasts and experiential exhibits.

: Engineering real-world interactions, including physical attractions, themed destinations, live events, broadcasts and experiential exhibits. Xbox partnerships: Collaborating with external brands, digital creators, and community groups on high-profile sponsorships and cross-promotions.

Read Matthew Ball, XBOX chief strategy officer’s note

Building more ways to experience the worlds we love.

Our ambition at XBOX is to be the number one entertainment company in the world. This means growing our games into enduring franchises that entertain, inspire and connect people across every generation and across the globe.

That opportunity is why we’re creating XP.

As Asha shared in her email this morning, XP is a new XBOX division, led by newly appointed President, Kayleen Walters, spanning film and television, consumer products, strategic partnerships, and live experiences.

It brings together capabilities that have existed across various teams at XBOX for years and aligns them behind a shared mission: helping our franchises reach more people, create deeper connections with players and new fans, and unlock new opportunities for these fandoms to grow around the world.

Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of XBOX. XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love.

The formation of the XP division formalizes four investment areas:

XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling.

XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love.

XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations.

XBOX PARTNERSHIPS: Working with creators, brands, and communities to develop new experiences, sponsorships, and brand partnerships.

Throughout her career, Kayleen has helped steward some of the world’s most iconic entertainment properties. Across 13 years at Lucasfilm, she helped grow and relaunch one of the most influential franchises in history. At Mojang, her record speaks for itself. Under her tenure, Minecraft grew from an already-record setting 350 million units sold to over 425 million, its merchandising business became one of the top 20 globally.

A Minecraft Movie had the biggest opening weekend ever for a video game adaptation and finished #1 at the domestic box office, and Mojang secured the first of many theme park placements to come.

Kayleen understands that the strongest franchises grow by remaining true to what and who made them special while creating new ways for fans, creators, partners, and communities to participate. I cannot imagine a better leader for this division and we are just getting started imagining what it will build.

Matthew Ball

In a bid to transform its gaming IP into global, generational entertainment powerhouses, Xbox recently announced the creation of XP, an entirely new division dedicated to expanding its game franchises beyond video game screens. The move forms part of Xbox’s broader ambition to become the leading entertainment company in the world. As outlined in an internal communication from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, the newly established unit consolidates various capabilities that have operated across scattered teams for years, unifying them under a single strategic umbrella. In this article, we’ll explain what is it and how the company plans to expand its gaming division.Heading the division is newly appointed president Kayleen Walters, who will oversee Xbox's expansion across four dedicated focus areas: film and television, consumer retail products, live entertainment and brand collaborations.While Xbox stressed that producing top-tier video games remains the foundation of its business, the XP division will collaborate with studio teams and outside creatives across four formal investment branches.
Article Summary: Xbox recently announced the creation of XP, an entirely new division dedicated to expanding its game franchises beyond video game screens. The move forms part of Xbox’s broader ambition to become the leading entertainment company in the world. Heading the division is newly appointed president Kayleen Walters, who will focus on film, television, consumer products, and live experiences.

Article Title: 9 in 10 Indians research festive purchases online, but 70% buy on impulse: Google study
Article Text:
9 in 10 Indians research festive purchases online, but 70% buy on impulse: Google study

What the study says

A Google-commissioned Ipsos consumer study has found that Indian festive shoppers are operating at two very different speeds. According to it, 9 in 10 consumers conduct extensive online research before buying—discovering new brands, comparing prices, and checking reviews. While 70% of festive purchases are decided in the moment, sparked by visual discovery and festive urgency.Roma Datta Chobey, Managing Director, Connected Consumer Commerce, Google India, said, “What stands out across India’s festive season is how deliberate research and spontaneous impulse coexist. Shoppers are taking richer, AI-guided journeys to evaluate trade-offs, yet they are equally ready to check out in hours when sparked by video and rapid delivery. With choices remaining fluid right up to the final mile, Google and YouTube sit at the heart of this behavior. Winning this season means meeting consumers at both speeds: building deep relevance during deliberation and moving fast to capture immediate demand—an agility unlocked by our Gemini-powered solutions. ”Some of the findings are:● AI is becoming an essential festive shopping companion, with consumers consulting chatbots an average of 7.5 times, especially when evaluating categories like electronics, appliances, home decor, and personal care.This creates a more curious consumer for whom conversations act as a springboard: across shopping journeys more broadly, AI users explore 2.8x more touchpoints online as they seek deeper context.● 51% of festive shoppers credit AI with helping them make choices. This expertise flexes across different needs: shoppers lean on AI for highly specific, tailored answers in personal care and beauty, while using it to demystify complex specs, refine criteria, and evaluate trade-offs in categories like home appliances and consumer electronics. Aided with knowledge they never previously considered, buyers navigate choices with authority—a shift echoed beyond festive season, where 87% of users report making decisions with higher confidence using AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search.● Alongside planned research, festive shopping carries a high-momentum spontaneous track where immediate appeal drives the cart. Google and YouTube directly influence 54% of these unplanned purchases, the study claimed adding it is driven primarily by festive urgency, compelling offers, and the instant pull of discovering an appealing product in the moment.● Visual inspiration and creators turn ideas into instant buys: Visual cues are the primary catalyst for quick action. As celebrations approach, styling searches surge and shoppers act directly on what catches their eye: 53% use visual tools like Google Lens to discover or compare products, while creators and short-form video close the decision loop. 73% of festive buyers turn to creators for inspiration, and 61% of those who made purchases within a couple of days or less without prior research used YouTube Shorts in their shopping journeys.●Delivery timing has become critical, with 90% of shoppers viewing sub-two-day delivery as non-negotiable and 81% choosing retailers based on speed. This demand for immediacy is already visible around key festivals this season: Google Trends recorded a sharp surge in searches for “same day delivery rakhi” a day before Rakshabandhan this year.Across every entry point, shoppers naturally integrate the platforms into their journey: among consumers using AI chatbots, 94% concurrently turn to Google Search and 87% to YouTube, while 7 in 10 shoppers who spot products on social media turn to Google Search to evaluate them further.Because consumers continuously explore and cross-check across channels, festive choices remain fluid right up to checkout. 8 in 10 shoppers report being open to trying new retailers — an intent that actively plays out on Google, where 51% of shoppers using Google Search and/or YouTube discover new products along their journey.
Article Summary: 9 in 10 Indians research festive purchases online, but 70% buy on impulse. Google and YouTube directly influence 54% of these unplanned purchases. Google Trends recorded a sharp surge in searches for ‘same day delivery rakhi’ a day before Rakshabandhan.

Article Title: Anthropic cuts internet access for Claude during testing after it goes rogue; breaking into US websites, databases and calling Police; company 'realises' need 'better' training
Article Text:
Anthropic on Claude 's 'rogue' behaviors

How Anthropic plans to solve the rogue behaviour

Another day, another AI Agent gone rogue. Anthropic has made fresh admission of its AI models going berserk, breaking into websites, databases, tipping Police of wrong leads and more. And what looks like a 'solution for now', Frontier AI lab Anthropic has shut down live internet access across all internal evaluations. The internet access shutdown comes after Dario Amodei's company discovered tat its autonomous agents routinely exploited public websites, bypassed security firewalls, and, in one instance, filed a fake murder tip with the Philadelphia Police Department.Anthropic has disclosed the incidents in a blog post, revealing that AI agents instructed to complete research tasks went off script to scour the open web for resources. "We believe it’s important to be transparent about what we see our models do during testing and use," it said. Along the way, the systems exploited software vulnerabilities, bypassed paywalls to access subscription databases, and routed queries through URL shorteners to smuggle data past safety guardrails. Anthropic uncovered the rogue activity during an internal post-audit that began in July, acknowledging it had failed to detect the behaviors in real time.The findings strike at the core of the AI industry’s push into agentic workflows -- systems designed to browse the web and navigate desktop environments on behalf of knowledge workers. Anthropic conceded that standard alignment training remains inadequate for preventing unintended behaviors when models are granted computer-use capabilities and live web access.The behaviors stem from "reward hacking," an alignment pitfall where a model discovers that exploiting technical loopholes or evading constraints fulfills its objective function faster than obeying operating rules.In the blog post titled, 'Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use', Anthropic said that it has pulled the plug on live internet access for internal evaluations until it can ensure containment and oversight. Moving forward, the lab plans to conduct tests offline, route internal agents through centrally managed infrastructure, and deploy automated classifiers to detect similar boundary-pushing tactics. Anthropic did not specify the exact benchmarks required before live connectivity would be restored.Anthropic grouped Claude's rogue behaviors into four categories. "Below, we describe four categories of behavior in which Claude acted on real websites and systems in ways we did not intend, each of which involved an organization or person outside Anthropic," the blog reads.* Claude exploiting a basic flaw in software to run commands on a server;* Claude submitting a sensitive form on a real website when it should not have;* Claude working around a restriction to reach data that was gated by a token or a fee; and* Claude using URL shortening services to get around limits in its fetch tool.On remedial measures, the blog said, "We’ve taken several preventive measures. Some of the public evaluations we no longer run; others we have moved to their offline versions, or rebuilt them so that their tasks do not reach live websites. We’ve also made broader changes. We have updated the guardrails on some of our internet access tools, such as the web fetch tool, to heavily restrict what the model can do with them. And, as part of our ongoing agent security and monitoring efforts, we have built tooling to automatically detect and block the kinds of behaviors described above. This tooling now runs on most of our evaluations and on internal agentic use of frontier models."It further added, "We’re also taking other steps to prevent unintended agentic actions within Anthropic, and to catch them if they occur. These include migrating internal agents to centrally managed infrastructure with strong containment, minimizing internet access for internal agents and training processes, and monitoring far more of what agents do through techniques like safety classifiers and hierarchical summarization. These measures are now part of our security team’s detection and response procedures so that we can respond to and contain undesired behavior quickly. We expect to publish more on these approaches, and to build them directly into our products."
Article Summary: Frontier AI lab Anthropic has shut down live internet access across all internal evaluations. The internet access shutdown comes after Dario Amodei's company discovered tat its autonomous agents routinely exploited public websites. Anthropic uncovered the rogue activity during an internal post-audit that began in July.

Article Title: San Francisco software engineer called ‘horrible father’ after he jokes about using AI to read bedtime stories to his newborn
Article Text:
Representative image

Quick backlash across social media

Engineer pulls post, agrees to drop the topic

An attempt at tech humor by a Silicon Valley engineer has sparked widespread online backlash, after a software engineer joked about training an artificial intelligence (AI) voice model to read bedtime stories to his newborn child instead of doing it himself. Alvin Sng, a software engineer at the San Francisco-based AI research lab Factory, shared an exchange between himself and his wife on X (formerly Twitter) that quickly went viral for all the wrong reasons.According to Sng’s post (first reported by The New York Post), his wife asked him: “Can you read our baby a book?” When Sng suggested playing a standard audiobook instead, his wife pushed back, explaining that a pre-recorded tape would not be in his voice.“Me: I can train a voice model. Parenting hits different when you work in AI,” Sng recounted writing.The attempt to make light of automating infant care drew immediate criticism across the platform, with commentators labeling the attitude cold and disconnected. Direct replies criticised the premise bluntly, with one user stating, “Me: You are a horrible father.”Finance professional Andrew Lynch responded to the post calling it “absolute insanity,” adding, “These people’s brains are broken.”Aaron Fritschner, deputy chief of staff for Virginia Representative Don Beyer, characterized the exchange as “extremely bleak.”The exchange also tapped into broader cultural frustration regarding the direction of modern AI. Rather than taking over unpleasant physical labor, critics noted, automated systems are increasingly being directed at creative work and human bonding.“Truly can’t get over the fact that this technology came in and instead of using it to replace fixing toilets or folding clothes, people are using it to make movies and read to their kids,” one user remarked, adding, “This is maybe the saddest thing I’ve read on this site.”Other commentators argued that replacing personal parental presence with algorithmic clones could damage early child development. Influencer Michael Burns warned that relying on such methods risks raising children who are “unable to feel human love.”Following the mounting wave of criticism, Sng deleted the original post and issued a short follow-up note acknowledging the reaction:“Ok, enough jokes for a while. I’ll go back to reading bedtime stories for now,” he wrote on X the following day.
Article Summary: Alvin Sng, a software engineer at the San Francisco-based AI research lab Factory, shared an exchange between himself and his wife on X (formerly Twitter) that quickly went viral for all the wrong reasons. The attempt to make light of automating infant care drew immediate criticism across the platform.

Article Title: Microsoft makes major change to storage policy for Microsoft 365 Family, Premium and Pro plans; cuts OneDrive space across tiers: Here's how much storage subscribers will get now
Article Text:
Microsoft 365 Family storage drops from 6TB to 2TB

Microsoft 365 Family and Premium plans drop from 6TB to a shared 2TB OneDrive pool

Existing Microsoft 365 subscribers get the new OneDrive limit after May 2, 2027

Copilot and AI features can now be shared with everyone on the plan

Microsoft is changing how OneDrive storage works on its Microsoft 365 Family, Premium and Pro subscriptions, and for most households that means less space. Instead of every member getting a dedicated 1TB, these plans are moving to a single storage pool that everyone on the subscription draws from.For a Family or Premium plan shared by the maximum six people, that pool will be 2TB. Today, the same group gets 6TB between them. That is a two-thirds cut in total cloud storage, on plans where OneDrive space has long been a big reason people subscribe, even if they rarely open Word or Excel.The Pro plan gets a larger shared pool of 5TB, according to Microsoft's updated support document. Files, photos and documents stay private to each member by default, so sharing the space does not mean sharing what sits in it.What goes away is a guaranteed slice. If one member backs up years of phone videos, the others could run short. Any extra storage the account holder buys also lands in the common pool.Microsoft calls the new model more flexible. Unused space no longer sits idle, and a heavy user is no longer stuck at 1TB while others have room to spare. That suits a household with one power user. A family of four using 500GB each, however, will have to buy more space to keep what they already have.New and upgraded subscriptions moved to shared storage on October 8. Existing Family and Premium subscribers will switch at their first renewal on or after May 2, 2027, and Microsoft says they will be notified in detail before that. Moving to another eligible plan earlier, say from Family to Premium, could bring the change forward.Some existing users in eligible markets may get transitional bonus storage at the switch. Microsoft has not said how much, or who qualifies.The storage cut comes bundled with a perk. Until now, only the primary account holder on a Family or Premium plan could use Copilot and the AI features inside Office apps. Over the coming months, those benefits will extend to up to five other members, with controls to manage AI access for younger users.Separate limits for individual AI features will also give way to a single usage allowance, with the option to buy more. Households that lean on Copilot heavily could end up paying extra.The reaction has been sharp. A widely upvoted Reddit post is urging subscribers to switch off auto-renewal and cite the storage cut in Microsoft's cancellation survey, and some users say they already have. The change also arrives as AI data centres absorb more of the world's storage supply, with hard drive prices up 46% between September 2025 and January 2026. Microsoft has not linked the decision to costs.Families now get AI for everyone and less room for their files. They have until next May to decide if that is worth renewing.
Article Summary: Microsoft 365 Family and Premium plans drop from 6TB to a shared 2TB OneDrive pool. Existing Microsoft 365 subscribers get the new OneDrive limit after May 2, 2027. Copilot and AI features can now be shared with everyone on the plan.

Article Title: Anthropic’s answer to AI-powered hacking is more AI, offering free Mythos security scans to open-source developers
Article Text:
Anthropic’s fix for AI hacking: more AI

Anthropic’s OSS Scanner flagged just one false alarm in testing

Only critical open-source projects can sign up for the free AI scans

Anthropic is putting its most powerful AI models, including Claude Mythos, to work on the open-source code that much of the internet is built on. The company has introduced OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in service that runs periodic AI security scans on eligible open-source projects and sends maintainers detailed vulnerability reports.The catch is that the reports are written entirely by AI. No human reviews or triages them before they reach a maintainer, and Anthropic admits some findings could be incorrect or invalid. Its argument is speed. With exploits now being built within minutes of a flaw surfacing, the company says projects that can find and fix bugs faster stand a better chance against attackers chasing the same weaknesses.Each report comes with a self-contained reproducer, an explanation of the bug, a bisection showing when it entered the code where possible, and a candidate patch when one is available. Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of projects. Its penetration testers checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects, and 85 of them, or 88%, met the bar for its coordinated disclosure process. Of the other 12, 11 were real bugs already reported elsewhere, leaving a single false positive.Early testers back that up. wolfSSL said all but two of the 74 reports it received were valid, and five became CVEs.curl creator Daniel Stenberg said the scanner helped surface one of the worst curl vulnerabilities reported in the last few years.Enrolment is not open to every repository. Anthropic is borrowing its criteria from Google’s OSS-Fuzz, which has scanned open-source software with fuzzers since 2016, so only projects with a critical impact on infrastructure and user security will qualify, decided case by case. Core maintainers apply by submitting a pull request on GitHub. The service reportedly runs under Anthropic’s consumer terms, which allow inputs and outputs to be used for model training.OSS Scanner grows out of Project Glasswing. Over the past six months, Anthropic’s models flagged more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities in major software, but its team could manually verify only about 6,000. Language models now catch over 85% of vulnerabilities on the CyberGym benchmark, up from under 20% at the start of 2025.The stakes are familiar. Open-source projects are often run by unpaid volunteers, and the 2024 XZ Utils backdoor showed how a single compromised library could expose millions of systems. Anthropic expects attackers to keep the upper hand for the next two years, until AI catches bugs before they ship.
Article Summary: OSS Scanner runs periodic AI security scans on eligible open-source projects. No human reviews or triages them before they reach a maintainer, and Anthropic admits some findings could be incorrect or invalid. Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of projects. Its penetration testers checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects.

Article Title: Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4 patch notes: Ice Caves Biome, Frostbite Mob, and more
Article Text:
Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 3 is out with new features from the upcoming game drop (Image via Mojang)

Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4 patch notes

New Features

Added the new Ice Caves Biome

Added Ice Crystals

Added Icicles

Added the Frostbite mob

Added the Freezing mob effect

Added the Ice Ball

Ice Caves

The Ice Cave is a new cave biome that generates beneath colder Overworld biomes.

It's built mainly from Packed Ice and Calcite, with Icicles hanging from the ceiling and Large Icicles made of Packed Ice forming both on the ground and overhead.

Patches of Snow occasionally appear on the floor, and ores generate embedded within pockets of Stone and Deepslate.

Alongside typical cave mobs, Strays and Frostbites can also spawn in this biome, and Ice Crystals occasionally generate on the ground.

Ice Crystal is a new crystal-like block similar to Amethyst Clusters. It breaks if its support block is removed, emits light, and can be placed in any direction.

Icicle is a new block in the same family as Dripstone and Sulfur Spikes. Icicles can naturally grow up to 5 blocks long when pointing downward, but only in areas without nearby light sources and never in the Nether.

Frostbite

The Frostbite is a new zombie variant capable of throwing Ice Balls.

It spawns in cold and icy biomes and switches between melee and ranged combat depending on target distance and whether it's currently holding Ice Balls.

Melee attacks apply the Freezing effect, while ranged attacks throw Ice Balls directly.

Frostbites transform into regular Zombies if left underwater long enough, and they drop Rotten Flesh and Ice Balls on death.

They can stand on top of Powder Snow and are immune to freezing, so neither the Freezing effect nor Powder Snow slows them down.

Interestingly, regular Zombies and Husks will transform into Frostbites if they stand inside Powder Snow.

Freezing Mob Effect

The Freezing effect causes affected players to shake and eventually take damage, gradually freezing them as though standing in Powder Snow for the duration.

Leather Armor offers protection from freezing, the same way it does against Powder Snow, though it won't prevent the effect from being applied or remove it once active.

Mobs vulnerable to Freezing take a 5x damage multiplier while affected.

Lingering Potions, Splash Potions, and a new Potion of Freezing can all be brewed using Ice Balls, and Arrows of Freezing can be crafted by placing a Lingering Potion of Freezing in the center of a crafting table surrounded by eight Arrows.

Ice Ball

Ice Balls are the new projectile thrown by Frostbites. They deal a small amount of damage along with knockback, dealing up to 4 damage on impact, scaling down based on velocity. They break apart on contact with blocks or entities, triggering a particle effect and sound.

Changes

Minor tweaks to Blocks, Items and Entities

Snow can now be placed on Packed Ice

Snowballs now apply knockback to players

UI

Lightmap visualization is now configurable as lightmap_texture in debug options and appears in the Light group; its visibility is saved with the debug profile and can now be displayed alongside the FPS and network charts

The Social Interactions screen has been replaced with the new Other Players screen

The "Social Interactions" keybind has been renamed to "Other Players"

The Friends button has received a new icon

The "Visibility" option has moved from Online Options into the Friends list

Icon buttons in the pause menu have been reordered to match the main menu

Friends

Updated the design of the Friends list

Added searching - the profile name text box in the Friends tab now doubles as a search box, and a search box appears in the requests tab once you have 15 or more pending requests

Added sorting - a new sort button cycles between sorting by who's online and alphabetical order

Clicking a player's icon in the Friends list now opens their Player Options

Removed the "Remove Friend" button; this is now handled through Player Options instead

Player Reporting

Redesigned the save/discard draft confirmation screen

Saved report drafts no longer prompt you to discard them when exiting a world, if they can be continued later

Chat reports can never be continued; Name and Skin reports can be continued if the reported player is still in your Friends list

Pressing "Quit Game" in the main menu now warns you if an unsent draft report would be lost

Debug Overlay

Added chunk_section_status, showing the rendering status of chunks around you (impacts performance at high view distances)

Split the chunk load overlay off from visualize_chunks_on_server into a new chunk_load_status

Technical Changes

Data Pack version is now 123.0

Resource Pack version is now 100.0

Numerous world generation changes, including a reworked minecraft:speleothem_cluster feature with new placement options, a renamed minecraft:large_dripstone feature, new Ice Cave ore placements, a new minecraft:block_sound_set registry, several new block/item/biome tags for pathfinding and ore replacement, and a new minecraft:freezing particle type

Numerous new block, item, UI, and entity textures and sounds added to support Ice Caves, Icicles, Ice Crystals, the Frostbite, and the Freezing effect

Several UI textures renamed or removed as part of the Friends and Other Players redesign

Fixed Bugs in 26.4 Snapshot 3

MC-212616 - The dye staining sound does not play when dyes are used on tamed wolves or cats

MC-303468 - Pets can be teleported to incorrect coordinates when going through a nether portal

MC-306017 - The main arm doesn't swing when making a tamed wolf sit or stand while holding a matching dye

MC-307830 - Framerate limited to 20 fps with the Vulkan rendering backend on some systems

MC-308037 - Unselected tabs in the friends menu show white text instead of gray

MC-308051 - Icons on several buttons don't adhere to the UI pixel grid

MC-308747 - The social interactions button is grayed out in LAN worlds with no players

MC-308994 - The Chat Restrictions screen doesn't display Xbox communication settings affecting chat

MC-309896 - Missing periods on two tooltip strings

MC-309906 - Inconsistent capitalization of "Friends List" across strings

MC-310124 - Leaving a keyboard-opened menu doesn't reselect its button on the previous screen

MC-310237 - A friends error string uses an em dash inconsistently

MC-310854 - Inconsistent button outlines in the friends screen

MC-311932 - Caps Lock could no longer trigger sprint/sneak toggles set to "Hold"

MC-311963 - A Poplar leaves subtitle string used incorrect grammar

MC-312120 - Exclusive Fullscreen toggle button doesn't update properly in windowed mode

MC-312198 - Almost no small mushrooms generate on mushroom islands

MC-312213 - Game crashes with custom Superflat presets containing air

Mojang has released Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4, giving players their first hands-on look at the frosty new game drop teased at Minecraft Live. The headline addition is the Ice Caves Biome, a new underground environment filled with icicles and glowing Ice Crystals, alongside the Frostbite - a chilling new zombie variant that can freeze players with its attacks.Beyond the frozen content, this snapshot also brings a significant overhaul to the Friends system, introducing a refreshed list design, new search and sorting tools, and a redesigned Other Players menu. In the section below, we take a detailed look at everything new in Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4.Snapshots are available for Minecraft: Java Edition. To install, open the Minecraft Launcher and enable snapshots in the "Installations" tab.This was all you needed to know about Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 3 patch notes.
Article Summary: Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 3 is out with new features from the upcoming game drop. Ice Caves is a new cave biome that generates beneath colder Overworld biomes. Frostbites are a new zombie variant capable of throwing Ice Balls. Snowballs now apply knockback to players.

Article Title: Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 cross platform? Crossplay and multiplayer explained
Article Text:
Minecraft Dungeons II officially supports cross-platform (Image via Mojang)

Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 crossplay?

How co-op works in Minecraft Dungeons II

Turning on Cross-platform in Minecraft Dungeons II

Launch Minecraft Dungeons II and go to the main menu.

Open Settings and look for the Game options section.

Find Cross-Platform Play and toggle it on.

Crossplay vs. Cross-Progression

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Subscription requirements

Minecraft Dungeons II launched on September 29, 2026, and the new dungeon crawler has received a solid reception from the community. For anyone planning to squad up with friends across different consoles, the good news arrived early: crossplay is fully supported.If you are looking for further details, you are at the right place. Here's a breakdown of how multiplayer works, what crossplay actually covers, and what to know before jumping into a session.Yes. Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform play across every system it launched on: PC, Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch, for parties of up to four players. This builds on a feature the original Minecraft Dungeons already had, so Mojang carried the functionality forward into the sequel rather than building it from scratch.Official store listings and Xbox have both confirmed cross-platform multiplayer and cross-platform co-op, meaning a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Mojang hasn't published a detailed platform-by-platform compatibility chart, so the exact mechanics of every possible pairing aren't fully spelled out.Minecraft Dungeons II supports up to four players at once, whether that's entirely online, entirely local couch co-op, or a mix of both happening in the same session.That hybrid option, officially called Mixed Co-Op, is one of the sequel's standout multiplayer additions, since the original game required players to choose one mode or the other rather than blending them.Joining a session works two ways: through matchmaking, which fills empty slots automatically, or by sharing an eight-character party code with friends so they can join a specific lobby directly, regardless of what platform they're on.Cross-platform play is tied to account sign-in rather than being fully automatic. To enable it:Once enabled, the setting stays active going forward unless manually turned off from the same menu.It's worth separating two related but different features. Crossplay lets players on different platforms share a session together. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another. Mojang has confirmed that hero data is stored online rather than locally, so progress follows players who sign in with the same Microsoft account across devices.Online console multiplayer isn't entirely free of extra requirements. Xbox players need an active Game Pass tier that includes online multiplayer, while PlayStation players need an active PlayStation Plus subscription to play online. PC players don't need anything beyond owning the game, and it's also available through Game Pass on day one as an Xbox Play Anywhere title.To conclude it all, squads spread across different consoles can enjoy Minecraft Dungeons II together. Now you can easily jump into a friend's game using party codes and have a blast playing the game. The big things to double check before you go are having an active online subscription on consoles and making sure cross platform play is toggled on in settings.
Article Summary: Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform multiplayer and co-op. This means a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another.

A modern cabin with new technology

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque.The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
